sec: Step 2 — the primary metabolic abnormality · p828

items.q: Step 2 states that the primary diagnosis is indicated by HCO₃⁻ and PaCO₂ moving:
opts: Along the line of the pH
Opposite to each other in every disorder
Only after the anion gap is calculated
items.exp: Step 2: HCO₃⁻ and PaCO₂ following along the line of pH indicates the primary diagnosis (the metabolic abnormality). (Book p828)

items.q: Match the step-2 flowchart when pH is DECREASED — 1) ↓HCO₃⁻  2) ↑PaCO₂  3) Direction of the pH branch … A) Decreased  B) Respiratory acidosis  C) Metabolic acidosis
items.exp: With a decreased pH: ↓HCO₃⁻ = metabolic acidosis; ↑PaCO₂ = respiratory acidosis. (Book p828)

items.q: Match the step-2 flowchart when pH is INCREASED — 1) ↑HCO₃⁻  2) ↓PaCO₂  3) Direction of the pH branch … A) Increased  B) Respiratory alkalosis  C) Metabolic alkalosis
items.exp: With an increased pH: ↑HCO₃⁻ = metabolic alkalosis; ↓PaCO₂ = respiratory alkalosis. (Book p828)

items.q: An ABG shows pH 7.28, HCO₃⁻ 16 mEq/L and PaCO₂ 36 mmHg. Applying step 2, what is the primary abnormality?
opts: Metabolic acidosis — the low HCO₃⁻ follows the line of the low pH
Respiratory acidosis — the PaCO₂ is the driving variable
Metabolic alkalosis — the HCO₃⁻ has fallen away from 24 mEq/L
items.exp: With a decreased pH, a fall in HCO₃⁻ gives metabolic acidosis on the step-2 flowchart. (Book p828)

items.q: An ABG shows pH 7.50, HCO₃⁻ 28 mEq/L and PaCO₂ 30 mmHg. Which two abnormalities are competing for the primary role?
opts: There is no acidosis or alkalosis at pH 7.50
items.exp: An increased pH branch splits into ↑HCO₃⁻ (metabolic alkalosis) and ↓PaCO₂ (respiratory alkalosis). (Book p828)

items.q: ‘In step 2, a rise in PaCO₂ with a decreased pH identifies a respiratory acidosis.’
opts: True — the decreased-pH branch gives ↑PaCO₂ = respiratory acidosis
False — a rise in PaCO₂ with a decreased pH is metabolic acidosis
False — a rise in PaCO₂ with a decreased pH is metabolic alkalosis
True, but only if the HCO₃⁻ has also fallen
items.exp: Step-2 flowchart: decreased pH with ↑PaCO₂ = respiratory acidosis; decreased pH with ↓HCO₃⁻ = metabolic acidosis. (Book p828)

items.q: All but one of these pairings from the step-2 flowchart are correct. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: A low HCO₃⁻ belongs to the *decreased* pH branch (metabolic acidosis); with an increased pH, the metabolic arm is ↑HCO₃⁻ = metabolic alkalosis. (Book p828)
